profile.story: Ray Fontaine bought two tractors in 2009 and now runs 19 power units out of Shreveport across a five-state regional footprint — dedicated contract lanes, regional partial loads, some port drayage. $6.21M of revenue and a 5% operating line. The entire routing, pricing and customer memory of the business lives in one dispatcher: Bobby Lynn Deschamps, nineteen years in, who works from a whiteboard, a personal Excel file on his own laptop and his cell phone. There is no TMS. Logins are shared, the dispatch spreadsheet has never been backed up, and Ray's stated problem is that he cannot find drivers.

intake.q2: We are an asset-based regional carrier. Nineteen power units, twenty-two drivers, running Louisiana, east Texas, Arkansas, Mississippi and the Gulf coast. About half the revenue is dedicated contract lanes for four shippers — food distribution, building products, chemical packaging — and the rest is regional partial loads, some spot freight off the boards, and port drayage out of New Orleans. We have a small cross-dock behind the yard. I sell, Bobby dispatches, Denise bills, Curtis keeps us legal with DOT.

blockNotes.b1: Ray opened with the driver shortage and stayed on it for twenty minutes. Objective is capacity; the secondary answer — resilience — is the one he gave more quietly, after we asked what happens if Bobby quits. Nine days away last year and it held until a customer phoned him directly.
blockNotes.b2: Five inbound inquiries a month, all quoted from memory, nothing captured anywhere. 30% close, loss reason is always rate. Funnel reconciles: 5/mo × 30% × $38K = ~$684K of new annual freight against $5.46M of repeat and contracted revenue = $6.14M versus the P&L's $6.21M — inside 2%, pass.
blockNotes.b3: Systems tour, and it is the shortest one we have run. The dispatch board is a whiteboard plus an Excel file that lives on Bobby's own laptop. Asked where the file is backed up: it is not. Asked who else has opened it: nobody. Watched Denise type a QuickBooks login that three people share.
blockNotes.b4: 27.4 h/wk of repetitive work inventoried, 19.5 of it Denise's, against an office pool of four people and about 160 available hours — 17%, plausible, pass. Bobby's 7.9 hours of load entry are the ones that matter, because that typing is the only place the routing logic ever gets written down.
blockNotes.b5: Cardinal Foods 21% on the revenue-by-customer report — a watch item, under the 25% overlay. The real concentration is a person. Also flagged: no backup of the file the company runs on, shared QuickBooks and Samsara logins, and two ex-drivers who may still have portal access.

P1.note: Three sources named from memory in q23 — shipper referral ~2/mo, load-board inbound ~2/mo, Ray's own calls ~1/mo. None tracked, no cost, no counts kept anywhere.
P1.why_not_higher: Anchor 2 needs volume at least roughly tracked; these are numbers he produced in the room, not numbers anybody keeps.

P2.note: Inquiries land on Ray's phone or Bobby's, are quoted from memory, and are captured nowhere. q24: 'Nothing is captured anywhere.' Response is same day when Ray is free.
P2.why_not_higher: Anchor 2 needs usually-within-a-day and some capture; the capture is zero.

P3.note: q24: 'If they do not call back we move on.' A second call happens when Ray remembers a name; no record of who was followed up.
P3.why_not_higher: Anchor 2 needs follow-up that at least happens person-dependently across most leads; here it is occasional and unrecorded.

P4.note: q25: ~30% close, 'no defined process, I have my way of doing it', no stages, loss reason always 'rate — somebody was eight cents cheaper'.
P4.why_not_higher: Anchor 2 needs a loose process and a rate that is actually tracked; 30% is a guess and nothing is tracked.

P5.note: Lane rate sheet dated 2023 (Doc), competitor-referenced. One change since: two lanes raised in 2025 after Cardinal reopened its rate confirmation. Fuel surcharge floats; base rates do not. q28: 'Unchanged for 2+ years' and 'Pricing is a current worry.'
P5.why_not_higher: Anchor 2 needs real economics behind the price and occasional reviews; with no per-load cost (see P9) there is no economics to price from.

P6.note: q29: cross-dock storage and drayage exist and are 'only offered if they ask'. No bundles, no premium service, no entry offer. Drayage is the highest-margin line at 26% and is 8% of revenue.
P6.why_not_higher: Anchor 2 needs add-ons offered ad hoc by the team; here the customer has to raise it first.

P7.note: q27: ~80% of shippers tender again within 90 days, dedicated lanes renew at ~85%. Both are rough. Inactive shippers are not identified and no reactivation has ever run.
P7.why_not_higher: Anchor 3 needs an inactive list pulled and worked at least twice a year; 46 shippers have gone quiet in 12 months and none have been called.

P8.note: q30: marketing owner 'Nobody', sales owner 'Me', budget $0, and leads/conversion/CAC/value have never been reviewed together.
P8.why_not_higher: Anchor 2 needs named owners and numbers reviewed at least sometimes; there is one de-facto owner and no numbers.

P9.note: Gross margin 22% confirmed on the 24-month P&L. q17: 'We know it for the company. We have never known it for a load.' No per-load profitability report exists — it was requested and could not be produced.
P9.why_not_higher: Anchor 3 needs margin by lane or service known and used in pricing; with 29% empty miles and no load-level cost, the rate sheet is priced blind.

P10.note: q20 'Monthly, delayed' — the outside bookkeeper closes five to seven weeks out; the 24 monthly P&Ls are on file and dated. Ray reviews when cash feels tight. One target: revenue $7M.
P10.why_not_higher: Anchor 3 needs a close inside 30 days and a routine owner review; neither holds.

S1.note: Freight decisions genuinely sit with Bobby and compliance with Curtis — watched both make calls without checking in. q50 keeps pricing exceptions, major sales, escalations, hiring, purchasing, banking, vendors and strategy with Ray.
S1.why_not_higher: Anchor 3 needs written decision rights across most areas; nothing is written, and money and hiring are not the only exceptions.

S2.note: q51 four-week test: trucks roll and billing continues for about three weeks; new pricing, spend over $10K and hiring stall; bank, insurance and four customer relationships stop. Longest real absence nine days.
S2.why_not_higher: Anchor 3 needs a named deputy and only a few owner-locked items; there is no deputy and the customer relationships are locked to Ray.

S3.note: Bobby quotes and books lane freight without Ray. Ray closes every new shipper and holds ~55% of revenue on personal relationships (q14); he is called directly when a customer is unhappy.
S3.why_not_higher: Anchor 3 needs the team closing standard deals with the owner in only on the largest 10–20%; every new shipper is Ray's.

S4.note: Two real managers — Bobby on operations and Curtis on safety — and Curtis genuinely owns the DOT outcome because the regulator forces a metric. Bobby owns the board but no number. q38: 'Mostly clear, with gaps.'
S4.why_not_higher: Anchor 3 needs managers owning outcomes and metrics; only the compliance metric exists, and it is imposed from outside.

S5.note: Two DOT driver-qualification files pulled at random were current — the regulator keeps that one workflow alive. q35: 20% documented, 10% current, 5% used in training. Dispatch, quoting, settlement and collections are undocumented; new hires shadow.

S6.note: q40 'Reactive only'; q39 no weekly KPIs, no owners, no visible targets. Ray looks at revenue per truck when the month closes.
S6.why_not_higher: Anchor 2 needs meetings that actually happen on a rhythm with a few KPIs; there is no regular meeting at all.

S7.note: Service is reliable enough to hold 85% dedicated renewal, but q31 says +20% means hiring and q36 lists missed handoffs, scheduling delays and rework. Consistency depends on Bobby being at the board.
S7.why_not_higher: Anchor 3 needs defined standards and QC steps; there are none outside DOT, and growth takes heroics from one dispatcher.

S8.note: Cardinal Foods 21% of revenue on the revenue-by-customer report; top five 54%. v2 anchor 1 is 20–30%.
S8.why_not_higher: Anchor 2 needs the largest customer between 15% and 20%. At 21% this sits just under the 25% overlay — a watch item, not a warning.

L10.note: q49: '$10,000, and I would need to see it first', Ray 2 h/wk, Denise 3, Bobby none. q55: 'Cash, staffing or leadership must be resolved first.' Real appetite, real money, no time from the person who holds the process.

assessment.owner_objective: Better operations and delivery capacity — move more freight with the equipment he already has, and stop being one resignation away from a shutdown.
assessment.owner_belief: We need more trucks and I cannot find drivers. Every time I get a shot at more freight from Cardinal or Delta Building I have to turn it down because I have nobody to seat. That has been the story for three years straight.
assessment.primary_constraint: The dispatch function is one undocumented person: the routing logic, the lane rates and the shipper history exist only on Bobby's whiteboard, his personal laptop and in his memory, so the business cannot see what a load makes, cannot price from cost, and cannot add capacity without adding him.
assessment.constraint_symptoms: Block 2: every quote is priced from a remembered lane and 30% close with 'rate' as the only loss reason. Block 3: the board is a spreadsheet on a personal laptop with no backup and no second reader. Block 4: 7.9 h/wk of load entry is the only place routing decisions are ever written down, and it is written where nobody can read it. Block 5: q52 names Bobby first, and the four-week test survives on him, not on Ray. Four blocks; the rule requires two.
assessment.constraint_cost: ~$214K of contribution a year lost to 29% empty miles that nobody can see at load level (derived from P&L fuel, revenue and mileage, Doc) · ~$34K of office payroll on settlement, invoicing and collections paperwork · 411 dispatcher hours a year of load entry that produce no record the business can read.
assessment.constraint_fix: Get the board out of one head and onto a system the business owns: a TMS or, as a staged first step, a shared dispatch sheet with lane cost per mile, a second reader, and a nightly backup. Price the dedicated lanes from that cost. Cross-train Curtis or Denise to cover the board two days a month so absence stops being theoretical.
assessment.momentum_initiative: Back up the dispatch spreadsheet to a company-owned location tonight and give one other person read access. It costs nothing, takes an hour, and removes the single largest continuity risk in the business before anything else is attempted.

opportunities.title: Reprice the dedicated lanes off a real cost-per-mile
opportunities.finding: The lane rate sheet is dated 2023 (Doc) and is set against competitors, not cost. Dedicated and regional lanes are $3.72M of the $6.21M P&L. Driver pay, insurance and maintenance have all moved since 2023 and none of it has been passed through except a floating fuel surcharge. Renewal on these lanes runs ~85%, and the two lanes reopened in 2025 both accepted an increase.
opportunities.blueprint: Build cost per mile per lane from the P&L and four weeks of settlement data, set a target contribution floor, and take the increase into the next rate-confirmation cycle lane by lane with the cost math attached. Cardinal is 21% of revenue and is repriced last, after two smaller lanes have proved the conversation.
opportunities.replaces: A competitor-referenced rate sheet that has absorbed three years of driver-pay and insurance inflation.

opportunities.title: Reactivate the 46 shippers who have gone quiet
opportunities.finding: 64 shippers tendered freight in the last twelve months; the customer ledger shows 46 more that tendered in the prior two years and nothing since. q27: inactive customers are not identified and no reactivation has ever been run. These are lanes the trucks already know and relationships that cost nothing to reopen.
opportunities.blueprint: Pull the dormant list out of QuickBooks, sort by the lanes the fleet already runs so recovered freight fills empty miles instead of adding them, and give Ray a twenty-name call sheet a week with a one-line note on what they last shipped.
opportunities.replaces: Nothing — this list has never existed as a list.

opportunities.title: Take driver settlement and invoicing off paper
opportunities.finding: 12.5 h/wk sits in settlement and invoicing from scanned and paper BOLs, both flagged for errors in q44 and both watched in session on Denise's desk. The same paper delay is why DSO is 61 days with $412K past 60 on the AR aging.
opportunities.blueprint: Driver-app BOL capture at delivery, image straight to the invoice, settlement calculated from the same record. Hours redeploy onto collections, which is the constraint on cash rather than on profit — the report states the recovered hours and the cash-timing effect separately.
opportunities.replaces: The paper BOL basket, the weekly seven-hour settlement build, and most of the POD chasing.
